results.title: Qatar vs Switzerland World Cup 2026 Predictions: Group B Decider
highlights:
Qatar arrive at this fixture as underdogs in every meaningful sense. Managed by Lopetegui, they have adopted a more structured, possession-oriented approach, but recent results have been unconvincing. Their qualification campaign ended with a 2-1 win over the United Arab Emirates, but they followed that with a group-stage exit at the 2025 Arab Cup, losing 3-0 to Tunisia and failing to score against Palestine. That kind of form heading into a World Cup Matchday 3 fixture against a polished Swiss side is difficult to paper over.
[...]
Switzerland, meanwhile, represent everything Qatar must overcome: tactical discipline, European club-level individual quality and tournament pedigree. Granit Xhaka at the base of midfield sets the tempo, Manuel Akanji anchors a back line that conceded just two goals across six qualifying matches, and Breel Embolo gives them a physical focal point in attack. Switzerland will likely be content to manage possession, deny Qatar space, and pick their moments to exploit the gaps that Qatar’s attacking ambition will inevitably leave.
[...]
Qatar’s recent competitive form makes for grim reading. Four defeats and a draw from their last five matches, with only one goal scored across their three Arab Cup games, tells a story of a side struggling for consistency and confidence heading into a tournament. The 3-0 loss to Tunisia in December 2025 was particularly alarming and highlighted ongoing defensive vulnerabilities against physically assertive opponents.
[...]
Switzerland’s qualifying campaign was exemplary: four wins, two draws and no defeats, with 14 goals scored and only two conceded. The friendly defeat to Germany and the goalless draw with Norway can be contextualised as rotation-heavy exercises rather than form collapses. Their 4-1 home win over Sweden in competitive football remains the most reliable indicator of their attacking capability at full strength.
[...]
- Switzerland to Win @ 2/9 – Switzerland qualified from UEFA Group B without losing a match, keeping their goals-against tally to just two across six games. Qatar have lost four of their last five competitive fixtures and failed to score in three of them. The gulf in class is evident in both form and qualifying record, making Switzerland the straightforward selection here.
[...]
- Under 2.5 Goals @ 5/4 – Switzerland’s defensive structure under Yakin is built around compactness and discipline. Qatar have struggled to score in recent competitive outings, netting just once in their three Arab Cup group stage matches. A tightly controlled Swiss win with limited attacking exchange is the most likely outcome, and under 2.5 goals at 5/4 carries genuine appeal.

results.title: Qatar vs Switzerland Preview 06/13/2026 | Forebet
highlights:
Qatar and Switzerland open their FIFA World Cup 2026 Group B campaigns with contrasting recent patterns, as Julen Lopetegui’s side seek control against a Swiss team that has been difficult to beat.
[...]
Qatar begin this FIFA World Cup Group B match under Julen Lopetegui with a clear need to reset their rhythm. Recent results have been uneven, and the challenge is significant against a Switzerland side that usually brings structure, patience and strong game management under Murat Yakin.
[...]
The more immediate form is less convincing. Qatar have lost 4 of their last 8 matches in all competitions, scoring just 0.63 goals per game and conceding 1.5. They also haven’t won in 5 of their last 6 matches, while their current streak shows they are winless in 3 straight games.
[...]
That scoring drop is the main concern. Akram Afif and Almoez Ali remain central to Qatar’s attacking identity, but Lopetegui may need more support from midfield runners if Switzerland control possession and force Qatar into longer spells without the ball.
[...]
Switzerland arrive with stronger recent indicators, as they impressed everyone in the qualification stage and Forebet predicts them to go as far as the Round of 16 before being eliminated by Portugal, who the algorithm predicts will win the whole tournament. Switzerland have won 50% of their last 8 matches in all competitions (non-friendlies), scoring 2.13 goals per game and conceding only 0.75. That combination of output and defensive control gives them a stable platform for a tournament opener.
[...]
One note of caution for Switzerland is their FIFA World Cup sequence. They have lost 3 of their last 6 matches in the competition, scoring 1.17 goals and conceding 2 per game in that specific context. Even so, their current all competitions form looks considerably more settled.
[...]
The midfield contest should shape much of the match. Qatar will look for disciplined spacing and quick release passes into Afif, while Switzerland can lean on Xhaka and Freuler to control tempo. If Zakaria adds ball-winning power, Switzerland may limit Qatar’s transition threat.
[...]
The forecast favours Switzerland because of their defensive numbers, stronger scoring rhythm and unbeaten run. Qatar have enough individual quality to create moments, but their recent winless trend and lower attacking output make this a difficult opener. Prediction: Switzerland to win, with a 60% probability of the final outcome, and the predicted score is Qatar 0-2 Switzerland.

Group stage exits followed in 2002, 2006 and 2014, each time frustrating exits that suggested Croatia could not replicate their debut heroics. Then came 2018 in Russia. Modric, Rakitic, Perisic, Mandzukic and a team built on collective hunger and extraordinary tournament nerve reached the final. They beat Denmark, Russia, and hosts England on the way. They beat England in the semi-final in extra time, Modric inspiring a comeback from 1-0 down. They lost the final 4-2 to France. Modric won the Golden Ball as the best player of the tournament. In 2022 in Qatar they reached the semi-finals again, beating Brazil on penalties in the quarter-finals before losing to Argentina and beating Morocco to finish third. Two consecutive semi-finals and three podium finishes in seven appearances. It is one of the most remarkable records in the tournament’s history.

Then there is the Modrić clock. Dalić now tends to pull him at around 65-75 minutes against possession-heavy opponents, and England are precisely that. If the game is still level when the captain comes off, the midfield control Croatia are built around fades for the closing stretch. Bellingham, for his part, knows this puzzle better than most: he and Modrić were team-mates at Real Madrid until Modrić's 2025 move to Milan, so this is the heir taking on the elder of the same midfield school. The one thing that should keep Tuchel honest is history. Croatia have spent twenty years winning exactly these games — tight, low on chances, settled by a single moment of nous — and this England project hasn't yet been tested by an opponent that knows its spine this intimately.
[...]
Our lean is a narrow England win, somewhere in the 1-0 to 2-1 range. We are not going to slap a fake percentage on a single 90-minute match — too much hinges on who scores first and on how long Modrić lasts. But if you make us pick, it's England by one.
[...]
The logic isn't complicated. England have the younger legs and the sharper edge in the final third, and Croatia's plan asks a 40-year-old to run the midfield for as long as his body holds up. So the result we'd least be surprised by, if England don't get an early goal, is a draw: Croatia keep it tight, Modrić pulls the strings for an hour, and the game sits in the low-scoring band they love. A Croatia win isn't far-fetched — they've made a career of these nights — but it asks their older spine to outlast a quicker England over 90 minutes, and that's the bet we won't make. Most likely match-winner if England do edge it: a Bellingham-to-Kane combination, or Saka finding a yard on the right.
[...]
England are favourites — FIFA #4, the deeper squad, and Thomas Tuchel's settled 4-2-3-1 with Bellingham at No. 10 behind Kane. Croatia at FIFA #11 have the edge in tournament experience and midfield craft through Kovačić and Modrić, but eight of their first-choice starters are 32 or older and Modrić's minutes are now actively managed. WTK Sports leans a narrow England win in the 1-0 to 2-1 range; a draw is the most realistic alternative outcome, and a Croatia win — as in 2018 — is live rather than likely. We do not assign a hard percentage to a single 90-minute match.
